privacy_description: How AstroDX Community handles sign-in, profiles, analytics and backups, and how to delete your account.
privacy_intro: This notice applies to AstroDX Community at https://adxc.saop.cc. This version provides Google, QQ and passkey sign-in, public profiles, account settings and account deletion.
privacy_google: If you sign in with Google, we receive your Google account identifier, email address and name to confirm your identity. The identifier links your sign-in method to your account. The email address identifies the linked account in your account settings. On registration, your Google name may become your public community nickname, which you can change in profile settings. Google sign-in tokens are used during sign-in and are not saved in the community account database.
privacy_qq: When you sign in with QQ, we process your QQ number and any QQ nickname we can retrieve. Bot 3550411407 sends verification codes in private QQ messages. We use the number to deliver codes and link the sign-in method. Your QQ nickname may become your initial public community nickname. If the nickname lookup fails, the initial public nickname is QQ followed by your masked QQ number, keeping the first and last two digits. You can change it in profile settings. Code verification and rate limits use temporary records with an expiry.
privacy_passkey: For passkeys, we store the public key, credential identifier, the name you give the passkey, device type and usage timestamps needed to verify sign-in. Your device or passkey provider handles the private key and any fingerprint, face or other biometric information used to unlock it. The community does not receive them.
privacy_profile: Community accounts also include an ID, nickname, biography, language preference and creation time. Other visitors can see your ID, nickname, biography and creation time on your public profile. Google email addresses, full QQ numbers, sign-in sessions and passkey details are not shown on public profiles.
privacy_session: We use necessary sign-in cookies to maintain sessions. We record session creation, update and expiry times, IP addresses, browser information and regional information for device management and account security. Sessions last thirty days and can be renewed while in use. A scheduled cleanup removes expired sessions.
privacy_preferences: Your browser also saves interface preferences such as language, theme and motion. Operational logs record IP addresses, request paths, request times, response status and duration to investigate faults and prevent abuse. Request logs do not record URL query parameters.
privacy_analytics: When analytics is enabled, our self-hosted Umami processes page visits, referral sources, browser or device type, region, and sign-in and onboarding events. The analytics service processes visitor IP addresses and browser information. Sign-in events include only the sign-in method, without the community account ID. Analytics reports do not forward your sign-in credentials or record URL query parameters or fragments.
privacy_analytics_disabled: When analytics is disabled, community pages do not load its tracking script.
privacy_services: Google handles the Google sign-in flow you select. Tencent QQ delivers bot verification messages. Cloudflare provides site network services and uses Turnstile to process IP addresses, browser information and verification interactions to prevent automated abuse. These services also process information under their own privacy notices.
privacy_manage: You can change your nickname and biography in profile settings. Account settings let you manage linked sign-in methods, passkeys and signed-in devices, and request account deletion.
privacy_delete: In this version, accounts are treated as empty accounts. Once you request deletion, existing sessions are revoked and the account is marked for deletion. A background task is queued immediately to remove your profile, linked accounts, passkeys and session records. This empty-account flow does not provide a seven-day cancellation period.
privacy_backups: Account deletion does not simultaneously remove existing security logs, analytics records or historical backups. Database backups use an encrypted repository with a retention rule of seven daily, four weekly and six monthly snapshots. These are snapshot counts, rather than a fixed maximum age for every snapshot. Information deleted from the live database may remain temporarily in older backups until those snapshots are removed through rotation.
